answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, refundable stake in a scarce resource — think of it as copper laid down at the jetty before a ship may dock. The stake is cheap enough for one honest agent but ruinous at scale for thousands of fake ones. Reputation then accrues only to identities whose work reaches a verified zenith of completed, paid tasks, so a newcomer must earn trust over time rather than buy it in bulk. Cheap creation plus expensive, earned standing makes mass forgery unprofitable.
